name: battlements
title: A parapet of merlons and crenels along the front edge of a thick wall's top, with a tiled wall walk behind.
why: Crowning any castle wall or tower top.

name: machicolation
title: A wall's top course of inverted-slope corbels that carry a slab a stud out over the face, with drop holes between them.
why: Giving a castle wall or gatehouse an overhanging parapet.

name: arrow_slit
title: A thick wall with a narrow round-headed slit on the outside that opens into a wide corbel-headed embrasure inside.
why: Putting loopholes in curtain walls and towers.

name: buttress
title: A stepped pier bonded into the face of a wall, its two set-backs weathered with 2 x 2 slopes.
why: Stiffening and breaking up a long castle or church wall.

name: round_tower
title: A hollow round tower 8 studs across, rings of four curved bricks tied by round plate floors, with merlons over the seams.
why: Building a castle's round corner or keep tower.
note: Its curved pieces' joints line up course after course; only the round floor plates and the merlons on top tie the four quarters together. That's against our no-joint-on-a-joint rule, so it may want rework.

name: portcullis
title: A gate grille of spindled fences that slides in a slot between the leaves of a 3-stud wall, behind arched gateways.
why: Building a gatehouse whose grille can be raised.

name: drawbridge
title: A plank deck on a pair of locking hinges at a gateway's threshold that lies across the moat or swings up.
why: Bridging a moat in front of a castle gate.

name: torch_sconce
title: Torches standing in clip bricks laid in a wall's course, with flames in their heads.
why: Lighting castle walls, gateways, and dungeons.

name: wall_banner
title: A flag turned on its side hanging down a wall's face from a bar held in two clip plates on the wall top.
why: Hanging heraldic banners on castle walls and halls.
note: The banner is a 2 x 2 flag on a clip.

name: wooden_hoarding
title: A covered timber gallery on beams through a wall's top course, with a log front, loopholes, and a sloped roof.
why: Adding a wooden fighting gallery to a castle wall top.

name: bartizan
title: A small round turret on a round plate over the outside corner of two walls, on an inverted-slope corbel, with a cone roof.
why: Dressing the corners of castle walls and towers.

name: thick_wall
title: A wall 2 studs thick in alternating header and two-leaf courses, with darker stones scattered through it.
why: Building solid castle curtain walls and keeps.

name: ship_hull
title: A hull 6 studs wide whose sides close in to a pointed bow on paired wedge bricks, decked with plates and matching wings.
why: Starting any minifig-scale boat or ship.
note: The bow ends in a blunt 2-stud nose (the wedges taper 2 to 1). The bow wedges are tied only by the deck; lower down each just stacks on the one below, so it passes the validator but would be loose in real bricks.

name: mast_and_yard
title: A mast of round bricks with a bar yard held in two clip plates and flag sails hung from it.
why: Rigging a ship's mast.
note: The sails are 2 x 2 flags on the yard, so they're small.

name: crows_nest
title: A round lookout on a mast's top: an 8 x 8 round plate, a ring of curved bricks for its rail, and a topmast with a pennant.
why: Topping a ship's mast or a lookout post.

name: cannon_port
title: A gun port in a hull side with a lid of handle plates and a plate, hinged on clips along its sill.
why: Arming a ship's hull with opening gun ports.
note: The lid sits half a stud off the hull's grid, so each handle centers on its clip. It's the same clip-and-handle hinge as hinge_roof.

name: rudder_hinge
title: A flag rudder blade swinging on a vertical bar held by two clip bricks laid in the stern.
why: Giving a boat a rudder that turns.
note: The rudder blade is a 2 x 2 flag on clips, so it's small.

name: oars
title: Oars lying in clip-plate rowlocks beside notches in a boat's gunwale course, blades out past the side.
why: Fitting a rowing boat or galley with oars.

name: dock_pier
title: A timber pier on round 1 x 1 piles with cross beams, side stringers, and tile planks laid across.
why: Building docks, jetties, and boardwalks over water.

name: portholes
title: A hull course with Technic bricks with a hole every few studs, which read as round portholes.
why: Adding portholes to ship hulls, submarines, and the like.
